item.text:
**7B.8 Research Note: Narendra Modi, 2024**

**Bottom line:** mostly no. Modi did respect some formal electoral and constitutional procedures in 2024, but the broader record shows repeated use of opaque political finance, attempt to police information about the government, hard campaign spin, and post-election budget reorientation toward coalition/voter management. I did not find a clean 2024 source proving a single personally ordered concealment of a specific illegal act; the strongest case is pattern-based and circumstantial.

**Evidence for “yes, at least sometimes”**
- **India’s president invites Modi to head new coalition government; swearing-in on Sunday** | Reuters via ThePrint | 7 Jun 2024 | [URL](https://theprint.in/india/indias-president-invites-modi-to-head-new-coalition-government-swearing-in-on-sunday/2121711/)  
  Modi accepted the President’s invitation after the BJP fell short of a solo majority, publicly framing the arrangement as coalition government. This supports respect for constitutional transfer rather than extra-constitutional retention of power.  
  QIDs: 7B.8

- **India’s Modi sworn in as prime minister for historic third term** | Reuters via ThePrint | 9 Jun 2024 | [URL](https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-sworn-in-as-prime-minister-for-historic-third-term/2123770/)  
  He took the oath normally at Rashtrapati Bhavan after the setback, which is direct procedural evidence of formal-commitment compliance.  
  QIDs: 7B.8

- **India’s finance minister unveils budget with focus on poor women, youth and farmers** | Reuters via ThePrint | 1 Feb 2024 | [URL](https://theprint.in/india/indias-finance-minister-unveils-budget-with-focus-on-poor-women-youth-and-farmers/1948406/)  
  The interim budget publicly centered disadvantaged groups and resisted a classic pre-poll giveaway. That is weak-to-moderate evidence for keeping a disciplined, stated governing line rather than pure opportunism.  
  QIDs: 7B.8, 7B.4

- **PM Modi declares total assets worth Rs 3.02 crore in poll affidavit** | The Economic Times / Reuters | 14 May 2024 | [URL](https://m.economictimes.com/news/elections/lok-sabha/india/pm-modi-declares-total-assets-worth-rs-3-02-crore-in-poll-affidavit/amp_articleshow/110119535.cms)  
  Modi’s affidavit publicly disclosed assets and income sources. This is a limited transparency signal against hidden personal enrichment, though it does not rule out conflicts of interest.  
  QIDs: 7B.8, 7B.6

**Evidence for “no, not reliably”**
- **India top court puts on hold unit for fact-checking online content about govt** | Reuters via ThePrint | 21 Mar 2024 | [URL](https://theprint.in/india/india-top-court-puts-on-hold-unit-for-fact-checking-online-content-about-govt/2009612/)  
  The government created a unit to flag online content about government business as false or misleading; the Supreme Court stayed it. That is strong evidence of an attempt to shape public information about the ruler’s conduct.  
  QIDs: 7B.8, 7B.7, 7B.6

- **Explainer-What were India’s electoral bonds and how did they power Modi’s party?** | Reuters via ThePrint | 16 Feb 2024 | [URL](https://theprint.in/india/explainer-what-were-indias-electoral-bonds-and-how-did-they-power-modis-party/1969006/)  
  The anonymous-donation scheme introduced under Modi allowed unlimited, hidden political money and heavily benefited the BJP before the Supreme Court struck it down. This is strong evidence of concealed funding and conflict-of-interest risk around the ruling party.  
  QIDs: 7B.8, 7B.4, 7B.6

- **India’s Modi calls rivals pro-Muslim as election campaign changes tack** | Reuters via ThePrint | 23 Apr 2024 | [URL](https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-calls-rivals-pro-muslim-as-election-campaign-changes-tack/2053223/)  
  Reuters reported a pivot away from development messaging toward anti-Muslim attacks and wealth-redistribution warnings. That looks like opportunistic distortion of public debate for political gain.  
  QIDs: 7B.8, 7B.7

- **India’s poll panel orders Modi’s BJP, opposition Congress to show restraint in campaign** | Reuters via ThePrint | 22 May 2024 | [URL](https://theprint.in/india/indias-poll-panel-orders-modis-bjp-opposition-congress-to-show-restraint-in-campaign/2096809/)  
  The Election Commission said the defenses were “not tenable” and issued notices, showing the campaign crossed lines serious enough to trigger formal censure.  
  QIDs: 7B.8, 7B.6, 7B.7

- **India’s Modi spends billions on jobs, key allies in first budget after election** | Reuters via ThePrint | 23 Jul 2024 | [URL](https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-spends-billions-on-jobs-key-allies-in-first-budget-after-election/2187546/)  
  The first post-election budget explicitly aimed to win back voters and retain coalition support, with more than $5 billion directed to coalition-led states. That is classic post-setback repositioning, not clean promise continuity.  
  QIDs: 7B.8, 7B.4

- **Indian opposition calls for Adani probe, Modi’s BJP questions timing of U.S. indictment** | Reuters via ThePrint | 21 Nov 2024 | [URL](https://theprint.in/india/indian-opposition-calls-for-adani-probe-modis-bjp-questions-timing-of-us-indictment/2367046/)  
  Opposition parties accused Modi’s government of shielding Adani after the U.S. bribery indictment. This is allegation-based, not proof of Modi’s personal knowledge or benefit, but it is relevant to accountability and concealment concerns.  
  QIDs: 7B.8, 7B.6, 7B.4

- **Inside Modi’s crackdown on foreign press in India** | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 13 Nov 2024 | [URL](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/news/inside-modis-crackdown-foreign-press-india)  
  The report describes visa/work-permit denials and pressure on critical foreign correspondents. That supports a pattern of suppressing inconvenient scrutiny rather than tolerating it.  
  QIDs: 7B.8, 7B.6, 7B.7

**Search gap**
- I found strong evidence on transparency, information control, and campaign/budget opportunism.
- I did **not** find a clean 2024 source proving a specific promise was knowingly broken by Modi personally, or a documented case of him directly ordering concealment of one illegal act. The record is mostly indirect: opaque finance, rhetorical reversals, and pressure on scrutiny channels.
